subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput A/B test
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput A/B test

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

What we heard from you
- Primary goal: ensure Redwood meets Globex p95/p99 latency SLOs for your real-time inference use case (short prompts, average req size ~250 tokens).
- Secondary goal: confirm tokens/sec throughput under sustained concurrency (200 concurrent sessions) vs your current hyperscaler endpoint.
- Procurement/contract timeline: aiming for a pilot by early September; procurement team needs a short technical appendix and A/B test results.

Redwood proposal
1) Run a controlled A/B test: identical request stream routed to Redwood and your hyperscaler endpoints. Two 1-hour runs (morning & afternoon) to capture warm/steady-state.
2) Metrics we'll capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (per-token and end-to-end), tokens/sec (aggregate and per-worker), error rate, and resource utilization.
3) Config: we recommend 8k sequence, batching up to 16, KV/cache warm-up of 30s per run. We'll provide a config file and a short README.
4) Deliverables: raw traces, CSV of per-request latencies, p95/p99 summary, and a dashboard link.

Next steps
- Can you share the test corpus (or a 1k request sample) + any auth we need to hit the hyperscaler endpoint?
- Are you available for the actual runs on Tues 8/25 or Wed 8/26 AM (PDT)?
- I'll attach the config + readme we discussed. Rafael is looped in for instrumentation.

Attachments: redwood_abtest_readme.pdf, abtest_config.yaml

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput A/B test

Thanks Marissa — this matches my notes. A few quick clarifications: 

- For the hyperscaler endpoint we'll provide an API key and a short-run load balancer URL; I'll coordinate with platform to share credentials (can we use a temp key scoped to the test?).
- Warm-up: we want a 5-10 minute warm-up plus your KV/cache suggestion of 30s; please document both so procurement can reproduce.
- Hardware parity: can you confirm the hardware you're comparing on (e.g., H100 vs A100) and whether quantization will be used for either side during the test? We need to annotate that in the appendix.

I'm available for the runs on Wed 8/26 AM (PDT). Please send the sample corpus (or we can export from our telemetry) and the config.

— Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform, Globex Inc.
alex.johnson@globex.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput A/B test

Alex — great, thanks. A few specifics and answers to your questions (quoted below):

> Warm-up: we want a 5-10 minute warm-up plus your KV/cache suggestion of 30s; please document both so procurement can reproduce.
- We'll do a 10-minute connection and model warm-up followed by a 30s KV/cache prefill per run. Note in the README how to reproduce the steps.

> Hardware parity: can you confirm the hardware you're comparing on (e.g., H100 vs A100) and whether quantization will be used for either side during the test?
- Redwood will run on H100 (our Dedicated pilot pool) with FP16/INT8 options available. For the baseline comparison we recommend matching the hyperscaler instance family as closely as possible. For transparency we'll run two sub-runs: FP16 baseline and INT8 quantized (if your inference stack supports it). We'll annotate which numeric mode was used for each CSV.

Attached: abtest_config.yaml (includes batch sizes, concurrency, sequence lengths) and redwood_abtest_readme.pdf (runbook + exact metrics definitions). Also attaching a results template we'll use for the deliverable: abtest-results-template.csv.

Quick run outline (for the runbook):
- Step 0: exchange API keys (temp scope) and confirm test endpoints.
- Step 1: 10m warm-up (connections + model load) for each side.
- Step 2: 30s KV/cache prefill.
- Step 3: 1-hour steady-state run (collect per-request latencies).
- Step 4: break, then repeat for second 1-hour run later in the day.

I'll schedule the runs for Wed 2026-08-26 09:00 PDT (primary) and 14:00 PDT (secondary). Rafael will instrument tracing and provide the CSV.

Attachments: redwood_abtest_readme.pdf, abtest_config.yaml, abtest-results-template.csv

Best — Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput A/B test

Looping in a few instrumentation details from the infra side so expectations are clear: 

- Latency definitions: our CSV will include per-request start/end timestamps, tokens emitted, and both end-to-end and per-token latency. p95/p99 will be computed on end-to-end latencies; we'll also provide a per-token p99 as requested.
- Tokens/sec: we'll report both aggregate tokens/sec across the cluster and per-worker tokens/sec distributions (95th/99th percentiles).
- Loss of tail signals: we'll attach raw traces for 1-minute windows around p99 spikes to help root cause.
- Versioning: we'll tag each run with model version + numeric mode (FP16/INT8) + kernel selection details so results are reproducible.

Attachment: abtest-results-template.csv (CSV header + example row).

If you want, we can also push a one-click Grafana dashboard link (read-only) after the first run so your platform team can validate in near real-time.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Head of Infra Instrumentation, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Please send the DocuSign/SDR paperwork for the pilot engagement and we'll route to procurement. Otherwise, ready to go on Wednesday — appreciate the thoroughness.

— Alex
